 Need a REAL ID before the holidays? N.J. says you can get an appointment in 3 days.
 NJ.com Follow Lia Opperman, NJ.com Express Desk Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:13 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:13 PM UTC With Thanksgiving travel around the corner, New Jersey residents who still need a REAL ID can get an appointment quickly, state officials said.
 The average wait for a REAL ID appointment at New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission locations is now three days, down from 73 days at the start of the year, according to Gov. Mikie Sherrill 's office. That's a 96% drop.
 The agency has issued 750,000 REAL IDs this year and is approaching 1 million.
 Advertisement Advertisement "New Jerseyans were waiting an average of 73 days for a REAL ID appointment, and that was unacceptable," Sherrill said in a statement. "We made operational improvements at the MVC, and now residents can get an appointment in just three days as they prepare for holiday travel."
 Acting MVC Chief Administrator Rosalie Johnson said the agency addressed capacity changes "by working smarter, not spending more."
 The state credits three changes. The MVC now accepts digital proof of residency, such as electronic bank statements, utility statements and pay stubs, which officials said have cut failed transactions and repeat visits in half.
 The agency also streamlined document verification and it added more appointments systemwide, including REAL ID services at seven more agencies this year.
 Advertisement Advertisement As of May 2025, the Transportation Security Administration requires a REAL ID-compliant license or ID to board domestic flights. Travelers without a REAL ID-compliant license or ID will be turned away at airport security checkpoints.
 You don't need a REAL ID to fly if you have another TSA-approved ID, such as a valid U.S. passport, passport card or military ID.
 To get a REAL ID, you'll need to bring:
 Two proofs of N.J. residency. Options include a utility bill, bank statement or mortgage or lease. These can now be on paper or on a phone or tablet.
 Your Social Security number. The MVC verifies it with the Social Security Administration. If that fails, bring a Social Security card, W-2 or pay stub showing the full number.
 Proof of identity. This means a primary document, such as a U.S. passport or certified birth certificate, plus secondary documents that add up to 6 REAL ID points. These must be originals or certified copies.
 Advertisement Advertisement Appointments can be booked through the MVC's online scheduler .
 If your license or ID expires within three months, you can upgrade at a renewal appointment. The MVC recommends using its online checklist or document selector first to make sure you have everything.
 At the appointment, staff will check your documents, take your photo and give you a temporary paper license. Your REAL ID will arrive by mail within two weeks.
 The fee is $35 for a four-year license or ID or $11 if you upgrade to a REAL ID before your current license or ID is due for renewal.
 For more information, go to NJMVC.gov.
